note: The closest thing in this batch to the ICP as Primal states it, and it failed on the one criterion that a payment plan is supposed to solve. He is a business owner in the literal sense — co-founder of a tequila brand with a distillery in Mexico and new operations in Madrid, five owners holding 90%. Health is precisely the neglected area rather than a crisis, and he says so in the ICP's own language: 'it wasn't a priority... it was building the business.' He is good wanting great, not rescue: already 22 lb down since April under his own steam, eating well, training four times a week, targeting 190-195 lb. And he is emphatically not the deconditioned exclusion — a college sprint scholarship athlete doing heart-rate-zone interval sessions. The single miss is income, and only on the affordability test: the valuation is strong but he takes a deliberately low salary, has no savings to tap and set a budget of about $500. This is the third data point for the observation already recorded in the ICP file, that 'makes good money' is doing work a payment plan should be doing — except here the plan offered was third-party consumer credit at a total above the cash price, and he still walked. The instructive detail is that he passes four of five criteria and was not closed, while a prospect who passes none of them was closed at full price elsewhere in this corpus.
